clue.text: It’s important you make this call

definitions.text: It’s important you make this call

blocks.clueFragment: It’s important you make this call
blocks.note: surface reading: a pep talk telling someone a big phone call or choice rests on them
setter's reading: a call is a ruling, and an important one marks a turning point

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a ruling of historic significance; 'call' means a judgement, as an umpire makes one.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling that changes the course of law or history is described as a milestone judgement of outstanding significance.

clue.text: Robots start to assist university doing a test on car wheels

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
to wheel is to turn round, so the phrase it follows is read backwards

blocks.note: opening letter of assist
standard abbreviation for university
at, as in 'at work', means engaged in doing
taken as written
the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for vehicles

explanation.surface: A student helps out while a car has its wheels inspected, and robots are somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'doing a test on car' is turned round, after A and U are in place. The MOT is the yearly check every older British car must pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Automata is the plural of automaton, a self-operating machine, which is what a robot is.

clue.text: Dictator, staying in the region of bar, sorry for picking up material

indicators.note: something staying in a place sits inside it, so the dictator's title surrounds what follows
in a down entry picking something up lifts it, so the words are read from bottom to top
this phrase is itself the Latin abbreviation for about, which here wraps around the words that follow it

blocks.note: Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, Italy's fascist dictator
ca, short for circa, means about or approximately
bar and less both mean minus or except
eh? or sorry? is what you say when you did not catch something

explanation.surface: A dictator sits in a bar apologising, apparently while buying some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub but means except, and 'sorry' is the puzzled interjection of someone who missed what was said. Mussolini was styled Il Duce.
explanation.definitionFit: Duchesse lace is a Flemish bobbin lace with bold floral sprays, a fine textile or fabric.

clue.text: Recommend Mr B’s predecessor for lifting depression

indicators.note: lifting in a down entry raises the letters so they read upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: to tip a horse or a candidate is to recommend it
in alphabetical order Mr A comes just before Mr B

explanation.surface: Someone advises a dose of the boss's forerunner to cheer up a gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' wants to mean low spirits, but here it is a hollow in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollow under the shoulder where arm meets body is a physical depression, a sunken area of skin.

clue.text: Eurovision winning song’s sound reworked in style of Spooner number

indicators.note: the sound a thing makes is used for its noise, a word which also means a telephone call
the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial consonants change places

blocks.note: a ring is a sound, as of a bell
The Code by Nemo won the Eurovision Song Contest in 2024
swap opening consonant sounds between first and last words

explanation.surface: A Eurovision champion's tune gets remixed in the manner of a famously tongue-tied Oxford don.
explanation.walkthrough: Ring of The Code is the sound of the 2024 winner; Spoonerising gives Roger Miller's 1965 hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or musical piece, and Roger Miller's country hit is one such tune.

clue.text: Refined, first impression of Kate, ideally?

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the name that follows
an impression is an imitation, a version reshaped from the original, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: opening letter of Kate
taken as written for the mix

explanation.surface: Kate makes a refined first impression, just as one would hope of a royal duchess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First impression' reads as a single idea but splits into the selection and the mix signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladylike describes genteel, well-mannered behaviour, so it is a synonym of refined or polished.

clue.text: Strong partnership engaged in business

blocks.note: first meaning: solid, sturdy and secure
second meaning: a company

explanation.surface: A sturdy commercial partnership is doing business.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for something solid and unyielding and a noun for a commercial company.

clue.text: See 16
Visiting W3, one’s taken rest

indicators.note: something taken in is absorbed into a larger whole, so one goes inside

blocks.note: visiting a place means being in it
W3 is the postcode of Acton, a district of west London
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone visiting a west London postcode takes a break.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton is a district of west London whose postcode is W3; I goes inside it after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is a state of doing nothing, idleness, which is what rest can mean as a noun.

clue.text: Unframed announcement put on display about the Listener

indicators.note: without its frame, a word loses its outside edges, the first and last letters

blocks.note: a notice is an announcement pinned up for people to read

explanation.surface: An unframed notice about The Listener crossword is pinned on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famous crossword series, but here the listener is simply the organ that hears.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is an anatomical adjective meaning relating to the ear, the body part you hear with.

clue.text: Adjusted policy taking my age into consideration: hospital added US-style condition

indicators.note: something adjusted has been altered and set differently, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written for the mix
taken as written for the mix
H is the map symbol for hospital

explanation.surface: An insurance policy is adjusted for the holder's age, with a hospital stay for some American-sounding ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US-style' warns that the spelling drops the British A before E, as Americans do.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypoglycemia is the medical state of having too little sugar in the blood, a clinical disorder.

clue.text: Delegations sent abroad to apprehend politician who needs to pay the writer

indicators.note: abroad can mean all over the place, astray, so the letters are scattered into a new order
to apprehend someone is to seize and hold them, so these letters close around the rest

blocks.note: taken as written for the mix
Member of Parliament
one who owes money
the writer refers to the setter, me

explanation.surface: Delegations sent overseas arrest an MP who has a debt to the author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent abroad' looks like a phrase about delegations travelling, but sent is the fodder and abroad the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Empowerments are grants of authority to others, the same as handing down powers by delegation.

clue.text: Voice link cut by writer during Wembley-based fracas?

indicators.note: cut by means reduced by having a part removed, so the following word is taken away
during means in the middle of, so the remainder sits inside the next phrase

blocks.note: the Football Association has its home at Wembley Stadium
taken as written
ink is what a writer writes with
a set-to is a brawl or scuffle

explanation.surface: A broadcast connection is interrupted by a journalist during a punch-up at the national stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the writer's ink out of link leaves L, which goes into FA SET-TO. Wembley is the English national football stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a register of the singing voice, high above the natural range, so a kind of voice.

clue.text: See 5
Mischievous beggar needs to give over

indicators.note: giving something up means losing it, so the next word is removed

blocks.note: to beggar someone is to make them poor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky little beggar is told to give over, to stop it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beggar' looks like a noun, a scamp, but it is the verb; 'give over' is a British way of saying stop it.
explanation.definitionFit: Impish means like an imp, playfully naughty, which is the same as mischievous behaviour.

clue.text: Do what’s necessary to solve 24 Down? Carry on speaking

definitions.text: Do what’s necessary to solve 24 Down

blocks.clueFragment: Do what’s necessary to solve 24 Down
blocks.note: first meaning: in 24 Down a ... must be raised, read upward in its down light
second meaning: to continue a discussion where another left off

explanation.walkthrough: In 24 Down the waterproof is pulled over, raised in a down entry, so the instruction literally is to lift that word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to resume talking, picking up where a previous speaker stopped in conversation.

clue.text: People at large are what thug needs for excitement

indicators.note: excitement stirs things up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written for the mix

explanation.surface: Ordinary folk are what a thrill-seeking thug needs to have fun.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mocking term for the masses, the general population or common people.

clue.text: See 16
Source of spillage after the Rising Sun?

blocks.note: first meaning: whatever knocks a drink over
second meaning, read in two halves: rising is up, and the sun is something that sets

explanation.surface: A drink goes flying in a pub called the Rising Sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rising Sun looks like Japan or a pub name; split as UP plus SETTER it describes the sun itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that knocks something over causes a spill, so an overturner is the cause of the mess.

clue.text: See 16
Stock farmer went smartly around lion

blocks.note: ran means moved quickly
c, for circa, means around or about
a lion is a person of great courage

explanation.surface: A cattle rancher hurried away from a prowling lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smartly' means briskly here, not well dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranchero is a Spanish American rancher who raises cattle or livestock on a big farm.

clue.text: Is it omitted from tequilas in cocktail?

indicators.note: omitted from means left out of, so letters are removed from the longer word
a cocktail is a mixture, so the remaining letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bartender wonders whether something has been left out of a tequila cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the start of a question; it is the definition, as in two plus two is four.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic one quantity is another when they are the same, which is what equals asserts.

clue.text: Who’s dying from declamatory sermon?

blocks.note: ex is Latin for from or out of
pi means sanctimonious, and a rant is a declamatory tirade

explanation.surface: Someone asks who is dying after a long, preachy sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is a schoolboy shortening of pious, meaning priggishly religious.
explanation.definitionFit: An expirant is one who is breathing their last, a person on the point of death.

clue.text: Prescribed drug for Caroline, needing a boost

indicators.note: a boost pushes something upwards, and in a down entry that means reading it bottom to top

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
Caz is a pet form of the name Caroline

explanation.surface: Caroline is feeling low and is given an antidepressant prescription to cheer her up.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the name is raised; the word for stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Prozac is the brand name of fluoxetine, an antidepressant that doctors issue on prescription.

clue.text: Bears the finale of the poet

indicators.note: a finale is the closing part, so only the last letter of the following word is kept

blocks.note: Rupert is the cartoon bear of a British comic strip, and to brook is to bear or tolerate
closing letter of the little word the

explanation.surface: Bears turn up at the end of a poet's story.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Bear is a long-running British children's comic strip character; 'Bears' is two bears in one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Brooke was an English writer of war sonnets, famous for The Soldier, a celebrated poet.

clue.text: Pull waterproof over buttocks

indicators.note: pull, with over, means drag something upward in a down entry so it reads from the bottom

blocks.note: a tarp, short for tarpaulin, is a waterproof sheet

explanation.surface: Someone tugs a waterproof cover over their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' wants to be a verb in the surface or the definition; with over it lifts the word in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Prat is an old slang term for the bottom, the backside, which is another word for buttocks.

clue.text: See 5
Christmas story, long drawn-out? Not very

indicators.note: not means without, so the following letter is left out

blocks.note: a novel is a long fictional story
standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A Christmas tale drags on too long, though not by much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not very' looks like a reply to the question; it says drop V.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a French-derived word for the festive season, used on cards and in carols.

clue.text: Curse America after it cuts national song

indicators.note: to cut into something is to go into its middle, so these letters split the next word
after places the word America behind the result of the cutting, so it comes second despite being read first

blocks.note: a national anthem is a country's song
it refers back to America, abbreviated A
standard abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: Someone curses America after it slashes its national song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' stands for America too, so A appears twice: once inside the song and once after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ecclesiastical ban or a solemn imprecation, so a curse.

clue.text: See 1
